newsitem.title: FRANCE: French auto sector buoyant, Michelin rallies.
newsitem.headline: French auto sector buoyant, Michelin rallies.

text.p: Shares in the French automotive sector outperformed the bullish Paris bourse on Friday, with tyremaker Michelin leading the advance.

Brokers said Michelin, up 4.32 percent at 345.20 francs at 1530 GMT, was benefiting from a switch to cyclicals and a string of positive reports recently, including a buy recommendation from Merrill Lynch in late January, brokers said.

"These recommendations arrived just as the market was keen to pick cyclicals, and there are few quality cyclicals," said John Lawson at Salomon Brothers. Michelin shares have risen around 20 percent since the beginning of the year.

Analysts said they were not aware of news in the past couple of days to explain Michelin's latest gains, but said investors have been feeling relieved since the company said in January that it was not considering a capital increase to reduce debt.
Shares in carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen were up 2.5 percent at 614 francs after reporting a 5.1 percent in 1996 turnover to 66.17 billion francs on a 7.6 percent increase in volumes worldwide.
One analyst cautioned, however, that there may have been greater deterioration in the margins than the results suggest, as some price discounts may be classified as business expenses.
Another analyst cut earnings per share (EPS) forecasts for the group to 21 francs for 1996 from 31 previously, 23 francs for 1997 from 39 previously, and 42 francs for 1998 from 59.
"I'm feeling a bit pessimistic," she said, citing the 33.6 percent plunge in new car sales in France in January and the 43 percent drop in PSA Peugeot Citroen car sales.
Shares in car parts manufacturer Valeo, set to join the CAC-40 index on February 24, were up 0.13 percent at 393.30 francs after hitting a year high of 396.80 on Thursday.
It said this week that it had signed an agreement with a local partner to create a clutch venture in India.
Shares in French carmaker Renault SA were up 2.56 percent at 128.10 francs. Renault's new car sales fell 29 percent in France in January, but that was still better than the market as a whole.
